# Two Numbers for Every Atom

<!-- STEP id="z" -->
## Atomic Number

The number of protons in a nucleus is the **atomic number**, written Z. It tells you which element the atom is. Every atom with 11 protons is sodium, and an atom with any other number of protons is not sodium.

<!-- STEP id="a" -->
## Mass Number

The protons and neutrons in a nucleus are together called **nucleons**. The total number of nucleons is the **mass number**, written A. Electrons are not counted, because their mass is so small that it can be ignored. Helium has A = 4 and sodium has A = 23.

<!-- STEP id="notation" -->
## Writing Both Numbers

Both numbers are written beside the symbol of the element: the mass number at the top and the atomic number at the bottom. Carbon is written ¹²₆C and sodium is written ²³₁₁Na. To find the neutrons, subtract: sodium has 23 - 11 = 12 neutrons.

**Two numbers tell you exactly what is in a nucleus.**

But Rutherford's electrons still have a problem. A moving electron should fall into the nucleus, and in the next lesson we ask why it does not.
